Its presence here tells me what this page is. Not a lost memory of a real night that mislaid its paperwork — that is the charitable reading I extended to the grotto filing, and I extended it in good faith. This one names a borrowed kingdom from another author's map, which is the fingerprint of text generated to fill a slot rather than to record anything.

I am stating that plainly because the alternative is worse. If the archive keeps a page like this in circulation, some future reader will cite Rohan as a party operating at Shadows Pass in 1023 BF, and a generated placeholder will have become canon by sitting still long enough. *WAH! That is precisely how a lie with no author gets into a history.*

analyses.verdict:
My verdict: unsupported, and probably not a record of anything.

This differs from the grotto filing and I want the distinction on the page. There I found an absent source and gave it the benefit of the doubt. Here the text names a kingdom that has never existed in this world, which is evidence about the document's origin rather than merely a gap in its custody.

What I recommend: retire this page. If a recovery at the Shadows Pass hillfort in 1023 BF is wanted, it should be excavated properly — an event record, a catalogue with counts and materials, and named finders who belong to this archive. Then an analysis can be written against it.

Until then there is nothing to hold. No sherd, no list, no ledger, no year I can check. Only a sentence about stones being cold, which is true of all stones.

analyses.title: Frostfall's Moonlit Mysteries: Suspicion Without an Event
analyses.subtitle: A gathering force, a lunar eclipse, and no record that either occurred.
analyses.filed: Deepwinter 15, year 784 BF
analyses.summary: During a rare full lunar eclipse, peculiar occurrences were reported in the remote Frostfall Frostlands. Witnesses described strange lights dancing across the snowy plains, mysterious shadows moving through the frosty air, and unexplained hums resonating throughout the night.
analyses.thesis:
The text claims a gathering force disrupting the tranquility of Frostfall during a full lunar eclipse, possibly for leverage over resources, possibly as part of something larger.

Read that again and notice how much of it is hedging. A force, gathering, possibly, for leverage, or possibly for something grander. Strip the qualifiers and almost nothing remains — and there is no source record behind it in any case. Frostfall's moonlit mysteries appear in this archive exactly once, in the `sourceArticle` field of this page, pointing nowhere.

My thesis is that this is the purest example of the defect I have been chasing all week. It is suspicion with no object: the *tone* of an investigation, complete with veiled shadowy uncertainty, attached to no place, no night, and no person. *WAH! You cannot be vigilant at a mood.*

sections.heading: Every Load-Bearing Word in the Original Is a Hedge
sections.sourceAnchor: The prior text: consequences 'far-reaching, yet their impact remains veiled in the shadowy realm of uncertainty.'
sections.body:
Far-reaching, yet veiled. Possibly strategic. Perhaps part of some grander design.

*WAH! Possibly, perhaps, veiled, shadowy. Four coats of paint and no door underneath.* I have written a great deal of hedged prose in my career and I know exactly what it is for. A hedge is honest when it marks the edge of real evidence — *the spell may have found custody rather than Archie* is a hedge doing work, because there is a spell and a cottage and a mirror behind it. A hedge is decorative when there is nothing on either side of it.

Here there is nothing on either side. I hold the page up and the lamp shows through it. Remove *possibly* and *perhaps* from this text and you are not left with a bolder claim; you are left with no claim. That is the test, and it is a good one to keep: if deleting the qualifiers destroys the sentence rather than sharpening it, the sentence was never carrying anything.

sections.heading: An Eclipse Is the One Detail That Could Have Been Verified
sections.sourceAnchor: The event is dated to a full lunar eclipse over the Frostfall Frostlands, Deepwinter 15, 784 BF.
sections.body:
A full moon going dark over snow. Of everything in this page, the eclipse is the part that annoys me most, because it is checkable and nobody checked it.

This archive keeps three calendars on the shelf behind my chair and takes them seriously enough to have a guide about it. A lunar eclipse is an astronomical event: it happens on a date, it is visible from a region, and other filings from the same winter should be able to corroborate it. A single confirmed eclipse would have anchored this entire page to a real night.

Instead the eclipse functions as atmosphere — a moon to hang over the shadowy realm of uncertainty. The one hard, testable, falsifiable object in the whole document was used as scenery. *WAH! Somebody had a fact and spent it on a mood.*

sections.heading: Three Pages, One Defect, One Origin
sections.sourceAnchor: This filing, undercity_grotto_seclusion_incident, and ruin_recovery_1023_bf share the same structure and the same missing sources.
sections.body:
Three pages laid out on the desk in a row, edges squared. No sections. No verdict. A thesis of roughly a hundred and fifty words in balanced, agreeable, consequence-shaped prose. A source identifier that resolves to nothing.

Three pages with identical symptoms entered this archive together, and the pattern is more informative than any of them individually. These were slots, filled to make a section look complete, and they have been sitting in the analysis index ever since alongside genuine filings — with the same kicker, the same archivist line, the same seal.

*WAH! The same seal, the same gold letter, the same weight of paper as the real ones.* That is the actual harm, and it is not literary. A reader arriving at this section cannot tell from the outside which pages are readings of real nights and which are furniture. Every hour those three sit unmarked, they borrow credibility from the twelve that earned it.

analyses.verdict:
My verdict: unsupported, and structurally identical to two other placeholder pages in this section.

I could have made this page beautiful. Grounding prose is not difficult once you know the trick — put the analyst at a desk, give him something to hold, and the sentences arrange themselves. Doing that here would have produced a convincing essay about a night nobody can demonstrate happened, and it would have been the most dishonest thing I did all week.

What I recommend: retire or rebuild all three. Rebuild means somebody files the source event first. Retire means the identifiers go on a list of claims the archive withdrew, which is a perfectly respectable thing for an archive to have.

There is a moon in this filing and no ground under it. I am not going to write my way around that.

analyses.title: Promo Mario — A Sighting or a Sales Pitch?
analyses.subtitle: I found my own sentences on a stranger's tablet, and the account still fails the only test that matters
analyses.filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — later that night, after the Revision 2 filing
analyses.summary: I recognize my own article on the Wario Inc. tablet, so I will not call this account fake. I call it unverified and highly suspicious: three separate parts of the account insist on the same wrong year, tears are the easiest thing in the building to stage, and the account's best evidence is a Luigi who was not Luigi. More sources should make me more suspicious.
analyses.thesis:
The clipping is on my desk at a quarter past midnight, squared to the blotter, and I have read it four times. The tea beside it went cold somewhere around the second pass. I keep putting my thumb on the same three inches of column — the part where a man reads a tablet and starts crying — and I keep taking my thumb off again, because the ink there is already smudged from the last time I did it.

So let me be precise about what the tablet proves, because it is the only honest object in the account and it is being wasted.

The tablet proves readership. Somebody in that studio — the host, the writer of the recovered account, whoever produced those Alternate Versions pages and that one-entry *Fallen Maris* page — had my article. My writing about Peach's assassination, the Star Fountain reunion, and the man who vanished was on that screen when the host read it. That is a real intersection with my investigation, filed where I can verify it. It is also all it is. A man reading my article and crying is not a second witness to the events in my article. He is a witness to being capable of grief, or to being capable of performing it, over one of the most emotionally engineered documents in the archive. I wrote the thing that made him cry. *WAH! I am not going to count my own prose as corroboration. I have some standards, and that one is load-bearing.*

The account does better than fake. Fake would be careless. This is careful: three separate objects deliver the same wrong year, the account's one manufactured doubt is followed immediately by manufactured proof, and the only footage that cannot be argued with shows a fake. I have seen this architecture before, in the eastern-passage file — second shelf, brown cover, still where I left it. I am not calling it a lie. I am calling it unverified, highly suspicious, and built by someone who has read the same file I have.

And I want it to be true. That is the last thing I am signing, because bias filed late is the bias that wins.

sections.heading: The Tablet Proves Readership — Not History, Not Identity, Not Grief
sections.sourceAnchor: WAH! I recognize the tablet passage. It is MY writing.
sections.body:
I hold the clipping up to the lamp, because the column about the tablet is set in the smallest type on the page and my eyes are forty years old and out of patience. The passage the host read is quoted there in full, and I recognized it the way I recognize my own handwriting on a receipt I did not mean to sign.

The tablet's screen shows my article as the archive filed it — the man who saved Peach so many times that his name became a verb, the disappearance after eighty-five years of silence, Luigi finding him at the Star Fountain, the flight on wing caps. That is mine. Those are my clauses. I know where I put the comma. The account did not paraphrase me; it carried me into a foreign studio and showed me to a stranger before he wept.

So I will grant the account exactly one verified intersection: somebody in that building had my article. That is not small. It is the first time the Mario file has reached across the world's edge and been handed back to me with a stranger's tears on it. *WAH. I will admit that I sat down when I understood that. Not for long. But I sat.* It is also not evidence of anything else. Readership is not occurrence. A man can read about Peach's assassination and weep about Peach's assassination without the assassination being within ten miles of him, and without him being the Mario in the passage.

And the tablet is not finished with my work. The same device, searched later, shows an entry called *Fallen Maris* that begins: "This record begins with the tragedy of 955 BF—not when Peach died, but when Mario vanished without explanation." Somebody in that world has already rewritten my article. Not contradicted it — rewrote its central date and its central meaning. One device, two texts, and the account runs on the second one. That is the exact operation I accused the charred note of performing. It is not proof of a conspiracy. It is proof of a habit, and I have filed the habit before.

sections.heading: Crying Is Not Corroboration — It Is the Most Controllable Reaction on the Set
sections.sourceAnchor: The host read about Peach's assassination and the Star Fountain reunion, dropped his phone and wept. Asked whether he was that Mario, he offered a name—not a remembered journey.
sections.body:
I have the transcript open flat under my left hand and the clipping under my right, and I am reading the weeping paragraph out loud to an empty office to hear whether it sounds like a man or like a scene. It sounds like a scene. Cameras rolling for a pilot. A tablet handed over by Darian. A dropped phone. A cue, a prop, and a reaction, in that order.

Crying is the one reaction on a sound stage that costs nothing to rehearse and pays the largest dividend. The account controls every variable around the moment: the tablet is produced by Darian, the entry is my own writing, the reading happens in front of cameras that were already rolling, and the host is described earlier in the same text as a man who performs whenever the answer is missing. "He performed" is my own entry's phrase for what he does with a set and a camera. The weeping happens in exactly the place where a performance of feeling would be most useful.

The event's closing test is the sharper one: "Asked whether he was that Mario, he offered a name—not a remembered journey." The account hands me the question that separates a hero from a costume, and the answer it records is the one a costume gives. A name is the cheapest identity on the market. *WAH! I could teach a puppet to say it. I have half a mind to build one this week and file the results.*

I want to be careful about my own stake, because it is large and it is on the page in front of me. My article already contains the sentence I wrote while this account was still a headline: "I would like Mario found, even if it means another unbearable celebration without me." I put my finger on that line now and it is still warm. I want the weeping man to be the real one. I want my article to have crossed a world and meant something to the person it was about. That want is precisely why I am refusing the account. The most dangerous evidence for me is the evidence I am emotionally pre-sold on, and this is the most pre-sold I have ever been in this file.

sections.heading: Three Objects, One Date: 955 BF Arrives Like a Script, Not Like Memory
sections.sourceAnchor: Alistair also places Mario's disappearance in 955 BF. That is the year of Peach's assassination; the archive places the fountain meeting in 1039 BF.
sections.body:
The account describes the tape label, and the description is four words long: a strip of white tape under the monitors, hand-lettered, reading 955 BF and nothing else. No title. No episode. No initials of whoever wrote it. I copy those four words onto my blotter and set the clipping beside them, and then I start counting.

Three objects, one number. The tape carries the date and nothing else. The tablet's *Fallen Maris* entry files "955 BF — The Disappeared Hero" under the same year and opens by moving the tragedy off Peach and onto Mario. Alistair, who has the least to gain, recites the same year unprompted. Three different media, three different voices, one date the archive considers impossible.

Eyewitnesses do not triangulate like this. Ask ten people when something happened and you get ten years, most of them wrong in different directions; the texture of real testimony is disagreement. Coached testimony is the opposite — the script showing through the memory. I built exactly that comparison in the eastern-passage file, with a merchant who remembered the man with the mustache and nothing else about the day, and I concluded that he was either lying or coached. The Promo account arrives with the same shape: three witnesses to one date, each perfectly precise, none of them able to tell me the weather, the other customers, or the title of the tape. "955 BF — nothing else." That is a caption, not a memory.

And when the tape finished, the label was blank. I have never met an artifact that deleted its own identification at the moment its testimony ended. I have met plenty of stories that do.

*WAH. And I let the same number pass me twice.* I filed the clipping with 955 BF marked as a flaw — I can see my own pencil tick in the margin, right there — and missed that the full account treats it as a founding fact. Three objects did not give the archive a date to check. They gave it a date to adopt. That is the difference between testimony and a campaign, and I spent a morning on the wrong side of it.

sections.heading: A Second Mario Story Is Not a Second Witness; It Is a Second Chance to Overwrite
sections.sourceAnchor: Like the charred note, this is another story to test, not permission to replace the old file.
sections.body:
I get up, cross to the second shelf, and pull the eastern-passage file down by its spine. It is heavier than the clipping by about four pounds and about nine months. I open it on the desk to the merchant's page — the note about the man with the mustache, and my own conclusion underneath it in ink that has gone brown — and I lay the Promo clipping next to it so the two documents are touching.

Here is the discipline I set for the note at my door, and I am applying it to this account unchanged: do not ask first whether it is true. Ask what it is trying to replace. The charred note replaces years on a farm with three days, a death and a waking afterward — it does not answer the old file's timeline, it overwrites it. The Promo account does the same thing with more furniture. It does not explain the gap between the 1039 BF Star Fountain and the present. It moves the disappearance to 955 BF, the year of Peach's assassination, and thereby makes the gap irrelevant.

This is why a second source makes me more suspicious, not less. When a new document arrives in an old case and it is sloppy, I learn something. When it arrives polished, consistent, emotionally engineered, and carrying the exact date the old file said could not work, I have learned that the fabricator is still working. The merchants may have been paid. The journal fragments may have been planted. The timeline did not work. Every one of those old flags is still in the file under my palm, untouched by this account — and the account has simply moved the fight to a date where my flags cannot reach.

*WAH! Two documents, nine months apart, one desk, and the same trick performed with better lighting.*

The competing reading deserves its place. Two travelers from a real neighboring world may have crossed a genuine barrier, found a man who is genuinely our Mario, and misremembered the date under stress. I cannot dismiss it, and I will not. But even that reading must explain why the man's own world had been told the same wrong date, and why the tablet contained my article in one section and someone else's correction of it in another. A coincidence that precise is either a plan or a very good writer.

sections.heading: The Account's Best Evidence Is Its Fake: A Luigi Who Is Not Luigi
sections.sourceAnchor: The figure turned its head sharply. Where Luigi's face should have been, there were two hollow black eyes.
sections.body:
The figure on Camera Three is the wrong shade of green. Too tall by a head. Too still — not the stillness of a man waiting, the stillness of a picture. The edges of it flicker like a signal going bad. Then it turns its head, sharply, all at once, and where Luigi's face should be there are two hollow black eyes.

I have read that paragraph more times than any other in the account, and it is the part I trust most, because it is the part that admits it is fake. The observers do the work I would have done: they check the figure against the thing it imitates, item by item, hat and height and motion and edge. That is real observation. And in the middle of it Alistair says the only sentence in the whole account I would take into a hearing:

"That thing isn't him."

Four words. No date in them, nothing to triangulate, nothing anybody had to be coached into. Now hold the consequence. The building that produced a green-and-blue figure that is not Luigi is the same building where a pixelated figure with red eyes climbed out of a television wearing Mario's voice and Mario's catchphrase. The account itself refuses to file that creature as the hero — my amended record calls it "something that wears the name." In the same few hours, that world produced at least two costumes of the missing: one friendly and weeping, one hostile and glitching. The weeping host therefore cannot buy his identity from the building. It is the building's most common product. He has to buy it from a memory, and the account records that he supplied a name instead.

*WAH. I have stopped finding this moving and started finding it instructive.* If the Luigis of that place come with hollow eyes, the Marios of that place come with hollow patience. The account's own evidence is the warning label I was looking for, printed by the account itself.

sections.heading: Souvenirs, Photographs, and the Tablet Are All Descriptions of Documents
sections.sourceAnchor: The claimed souvenirs and photographs have not been authenticated here, and Peach never appears before the visitors in the account.
sections.body:
I clear the blotter and start stacking, because I want to see the distance as a physical height. Bottom of the pile: the clipping, newsprint, real, mine. On top of it: the full account, recovered the same evening, from the same source, ending the same way twice. On top of that: the device record I filed for the tablet, whose own note admits the screen contents were transcribed from the account underneath it. And on top of that, weighing nothing at all, the thing I actually want — the screen itself, which is not in the room and never has been.

Four sheets. That is the shape of it, and it is about a quarter of an inch tall.

My rule for documents is simple enough to fit on the door: if the prose says a document exists, the reader can open the document. Nothing in that stack passes. Everything inside the account is someone's word about something else. The souvenir shirt, the ticket stub, the soda can, the churro stick, the disposable photograph — described, never produced. The tape was never recovered; the account places it in Dr. Takeda's hands. The footage has no frame, no tape, no authenticated server record. I hold a transcription of a claim about a screen I have not seen, made by a man I have not met, in a studio I cannot visit.

*WAH! Four layers between me and the only object in this account I actually recognize, and the top layer is made of air.*

The paper reports photographs; it does not put a developed photograph in my hands. The claimed souvenirs and photographs have not been authenticated, and Peach never appears before the visitors in the account. Peach never appears. The account's most profitable claim — that she is alive and kept safe offstage — is also the only claim that arrives with no description at all, not even a bad one. Suspicion is not the correct response to that. Filing is.

sections.heading: File the Identity Question Last: The Only Testable Fact Is a Missing Brother
sections.sourceAnchor: No note, no struggle, no usable security footage.
sections.body:
The account hands me its own instruction, and I am taking it: find Luigi. Everything else in the filing stands or falls on identifying a host who offered a name instead of a memory. Luigi's disappearance stands on nothing. No note, no struggle, no usable security footage — the one entry in the account that does not require the weeping man to be the real hero. If that studio can produce a false Luigi, it can also produce a false no-signal; but a person is either found or he is not, and that is a question I can actually ask across a world's edge.

The second instruction is the account at its best. The narrator refuses the familiar exit, and Alistair confirms the pattern: "We did this with the door. This place uses familiar exits as traps." I believe them. I also believe the account would not have shown me the trap if the trap were only in the building. A story is a corridor; the obvious door in it is the next page. Do not go to the exit.

And keep the flashlight. The account's most expensive artifact — the Wario Inc. tablet, with a feature list longer than a castle's tax roll — defeats the Apparition by being a flashlight: "All it was," Darian says, "is a flashlight." *WAH! I keep retelling that line because it is the account's one clean lesson and its one honest object.* The grand artifact is theater. The ordinary instrument is what works. In this file, the grand identity is theater too. Chase the ordinary instrument: the brother, the tape, the footage, the separate interviews.

So I square the four sheets back into one stack, tap the edge against the desk until the corners line up, and put the clipping on top where I will see it first tomorrow. The tea is stone cold and I drink it anyway. Outside it has gone quiet in the way it does after two. Somewhere across the world's edge a man is either sleeping badly because he lost his brother, or sleeping fine because he was paid to say he did, and I have exactly one question that can tell those two men apart. I write it on the blotter in block capitals so I do not soften it by morning: **ASK HIM THE ROUTE.**

analyses.verdict:
Verdict: unverified and highly suspicious. Not fake — because the tablet gets my sentences right, and because I cannot prove Darian, Alistair, or the weeping host are lying. Highly suspicious — because the account's consistency is engineered, its date is a campaign, and its best evidence is counterfeit.

What the account is worth: it is the first document in the Mario file that lists what somebody wants me to believe, in three different voices, with the props to make each voice stick. That is a design schematic, and I am filing it as one.

What I recommend: treat "Mario" as a name with no memory behind it and stop asking whether the host is the hero. Take the account's own casualty list when it says Luigi: find Luigi, because it is the only fact on the page that does not depend on identifying the studio host. Obtain the original tape and the Camera Three footage — the account describes both and hands me neither. Interview Darian and Alistair separately, the way I should have interviewed the merchants: separately, about the weather, and about what else was in the room. Ask the host for one private memory the tablet could not have supplied — a route from the Star Fountain, a detail from before the reunion. Ask for the photograph. Ask for the churro stick.

And do not go to the exit. The account is at least right about the kind of trap a familiar door makes. If this story was built from my file, the exit is not a door. It is the next page.

The lamp is still on. The stack is squared. The clipping is on top, and the smudge where my thumb keeps landing has gone from grey to nearly black.

researchDesk.title: Waluigi's After-Hours Research Desk
researchDesk.intro: The verdict is filed. These checks do not test the account; they test me, and the three places where my suspicion might be doing the work instead of the evidence.

rolls.title: How far the account's readership goes
rolls.prompt: Set the tablet's own search result — Fallen Maris, 955 BF — beside the line I wrote about Peach's assassination.
rolls.success: Breakthrough: the tablet did not just display the article I wrote; it contained a second article that corrects mine. Anybody who built that screen had read me and then rewritten me. I will treat the account as a reader of the file, not a visitor to the story.
rolls.failure: Useful limit: I cannot prove who wrote the tablet's contents, only that the contents existed. "Somebody in that building read my file" is a claim I can make; "somebody in that building wrote a new file" is the same claim in a hat.

rolls.title: The one question the host could not pass
rolls.prompt: Take the account's own failure — a name instead of a remembered journey — and ask what he would say if asked for a route that was not printed in my article.
rolls.success: Breakthrough: a real Mario would answer the route question; a performer would answer with the tablet. I will make that question the single test and stop asking about the cap.
rolls.failure: Useful limit: I have one account of one conversation; I cannot make a man prove a life in one interview. The name-only answer stays suspicious, not decisive.

rolls.title: What the tape erased when it ejected
rolls.prompt: Compare a label that read 955 BF and ended blank with journal fragments that lost exactly the pages that would identify them.
rolls.success: Breakthrough: the self-erasing artifact is the whole account in one object — testimony that deletes itself at the exact moment it becomes checkable. I will stop asking the account to produce evidence and start asking what it wants me to replace.
rolls.failure: Useful limit: a tape that ejects itself and a label that changed are, so far, words from one source. I cannot file a mechanism; I can only file that the evidence describes its own disappearance.

analyses.title: The Lava-Bridge Ambush and the Blue Luigi
analyses.subtitle: Why the gate, the hinges, the axe, and the smile all point one way: the compound admitted ME on purpose
analyses.filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — night, after the session filing
analyses.summary: I did not infiltrate the compound that night; the compound admitted me, the same way it later admitted its own asset — and the three-step plan should be run with that reading in force.
analyses.thesis: I have the gatehouse passage open in front of me, and I keep returning to the smallest verb in it: clicked. The guard reached sideways without looking and clicked a button, and the most secure annex in the kingdom opened for a man it had just laughed at. I filed that as incompetence for years, because incompetence is usually the answer, and I have spent this week taking the filing apart piece by piece. The button, the hinges, the unmanned wall-walk, the axe waiting at the far end of an empty bridge, the smile that opened the same gate an hour later, the wall that burst outward, the repair order nobody filed, the silence from Bowser’s office: laid in a row, they stop looking like seven accidents. My argument is that I was admitted that night, not that I broke in — herded through a door the compound wanted me to use, toward a bridge it had already set.

sections.heading: The Button Is the Whole Argument
sections.sourceAnchor: You know what — he IS here. Second floor. Lava bridge. Take the warp pipe.
sections.body:
Start with what the guard actually did, in order. He laughed at my outfit. He told me I would not last two minutes in Bowser’s castle. He said Bowser was not in the compound and that I would not be talking to him. Then I slammed one hand on the window frame — one hand, once, no weapon drawn, no threat uttered — and the same guard reversed every position he held: Bowser IS here, second floor, lava bridge, take the warp pipe, and the gate began to open.

Guards who surrender do not surrender upward. A frightened sentry waves you past the checkpoint; he does not give you directions to the interior, name the floor, name the bridge, and prescribe your route. Directions are hospitality. Prescribed routes are herding. What I received at that window was not a failure of nerve but a change of script, delivered mid-scene, the way a man switches to the page he was supposed to be on all along.

I held the incompetence reading for years, and I will say for it what I can: the laugh was genuine, the boredom was genuine, and no actor performs disdain that good on purpose. But disdain and instruction are not opposites. The guard’s contempt was for me. The button was for whoever told him which visitors get the warp pipe. I do not think he was bribed or threatened. I think he was rostered — posted at that window with standing orders, a bad attitude, and one button, and I think my palm hitting that frame was simply the cue he had been told to wait for.

sections.heading: The Hinges Were Oiled
sections.sourceAnchor: The hinges did not even squeak.
sections.body:
Iron gates that stand unused seize. Anyone who has kept a building knows this the way they know their own rent. A gate that swings silently, on a cold night, at an annex that is supposed to be a sleepy backwater holding, is a gate that gets used — and used often, and recently, and by traffic nobody entered in any log I have ever been allowed to see.

Set that beside the wall-walk where nobody was walking. An unmanned wall above a well-used gate is a combination that should not exist: either the traffic is legitimate, in which case someone watches it, or it is not, in which case someone stops it. Nobody watched. Nobody stopped. The gate worked perfectly for exactly the visitor it was oiled for, and I walked through it congratulating myself on my powers of intimidation.

Maintenance is intent with a paper trail, except here the paper trail is missing — which is itself the trail. Somebody oils those hinges. Somebody rosters that guard. Somebody decided, before I arrived, that the correct response to one slammed hand was full admission with directions. I keep both readings on the file the way I keep everything: incompetence, or invitation. The hinges vote invitation, and hinges do not bluff.

sections.heading: The Axe Needed Two Hours’ Notice
sections.sourceAnchor: Just an axe, waiting, at the far end of a bridge over lava.
sections.body:
Down the pipe, across the bridge: one object in an empty room, upright in the stone, catching the light like it had been polished that morning. Nobody builds a room around an axe because they ran out of chairs. The bridge was set — and here is the part I underweighted for years — it was set on a timetable. Luigi reached that compound at most two hours before I did. If the axe was placed for me specifically, the trap had two hours’ notice at most.

Two hours buys astonishing logistics, or it buys foreknowledge. There is no third supplier. Either someone inside that compound can furnish a lava bridge on an evening’s notice — in which case the compound is far more staffed and far more ready than its sleepy-annex story allows — or someone knew I was coming before I did, in which case the button at the gate and the axe on the bridge are two ends of one decision.

I prefer the second, and not only because it flatters my importance. The first requires a compound full of busy invisible people who then all simultaneously fail to appear for the rest of the night. The second requires one informed party and a standing arrangement. The bridge I walked was not a room that happened to contain an axe. It was an appointment I kept without knowing I had made it.

sections.heading: The Gate Opened for a Smile
sections.sourceAnchor: and the guard opened the gate. Just like that.
sections.body:
An hour later I watched the same checkpoint admit the compound’s own asset, and the comparison is the most damning exhibit I own. My admission: three knocks, an interrogation about my outfit, a two-minute insult, a slammed hand, a button. The asset’s admission: one slow smile, and the iron swung wide like it was expected.

Two admissions, same gate, same night, same guard — and the asset’s was smoother. That ordering matters. If the checkpoint were merely corrupt, the stranger with no credentials gets the slow treatment and the known face gets waved through; what happened instead is that BOTH of us got through, at different speeds, with different ceremonies, as if the gate had a setting for each of us. Mine required a cue. Its required a face.

I filed both readings at the time and I repeat them now: either that guard runs the most corrupt checkpoint in the kingdom, or the compound knew its own asset on sight. I believe the second the way I believe in gravity. And if the gate knew the asset, then the gate’s earlier performance for me — the laugh, the insult, the button — was not security failing. It was reception, wearing security’s uniform, processing exactly the visitor it was told to process.

sections.heading: The Wall Burst Outward
sections.sourceAnchor: The entrance wall burst outward in a shower of rubble and dust.
sections.body:
Direction is testimony. The entrance wall burst OUTWARD — from inside, toward the road, toward witnesses. A wall breached by attackers falls inward. A wall demolished for an exit falls outward. What came through that wreckage, unhurried and humming, was the asset making an entrance it had clearly rehearsed: the confession, the comedy, the giggle at the screaming inside.

Then count the silences after. Nobody filed a repair order for a burst entrance wall and a missing bridge. Bowser’s office said nothing about the night at all. A breached military annex that declines to notice its own breach is either the worst-run holding in the kingdom or a holding whose night went to plan. I no longer grade that generously.

I do not claim the compound scripted every minute — no plan survives contact with Wario reversing a car into its lead performer. But a plan does not need every minute. It needs the door, the route, and the room. The compound supplied all three, then watched its wall come down and filed nothing. That is not the behavior of a victim of circumstance. That is the behavior of a stage manager striking a set.

sections.heading: Herded, Not Hunted
sections.sourceAnchor: the crew was herded, not hunted.
sections.body:
My own session note says the crew was herded, not hunted, and I wrote it about the impostor’s operation — the baited Mario lead, the helpful guide, the clues that led exactly where Bowser wanted. I am promoting that sentence tonight. It was never only about the crew. Luigi was herded to that bridge by shut doors: the Guild’s, and then every other door in the kingdom, until only the Koopa’s shelter and the compound’s pipe remained. I was herded down the same pipe by a button, a set of oiled hinges, and an axe I was plainly meant to find.

Three parties, three routes, one room — and the room was ready. That is the shape of the night once the accidents are laid in a row: not a collision of separate desperate plans, but a funnel with three mouths and one floor. Desperation with a borrowed axe and tradecraft with a rehearsed smile met on a bridge that had been set for at least one of them, possibly both, and the only person in the building who believes any of it was coincidence is the version of me that filed the incompetence reading. He was tired. He has been overruled.

None of this lessens what the night cost. A herded man’s burns burn the same. Luigi went over those falls carrying the only reading of the only paper that mattered, and no theory of admission gets him back or reads the note. What the invitation reading changes is not the past but the standing orders: we were allowed in once, which means we were watched throughout, which means the footage exists, the asset’s retrieval is already being arranged, and step one of the plan — the prisoner, before Bowser’s people come back for him — is not the first step. It is the only step with a clock on it.

analyses.verdict:
My verdict is that the compound admitted me on purpose, through a checkpoint performing security over standing orders, down a route that ended at a furnished room — and that the crew’s asset walked the same gate an hour later on the same arrangement, with a smoother ceremony because it was the expected guest and I was the managed one. The incompetence reading I held for years explains the guard’s manners and nothing else; the invitation reading explains the button, the hinges, the wall-walk, the axe, the smile, the outward wall, and the silence after, at the single cost of admitting I was handled all night by professionals.

I so admit. Handle me again and I will bring a bigger file.

Run the three steps with this reading in force: pull the footage first in spirit if not in order, because cameras that watched an invited guest watched everything; work the prisoner fast, because a retrieved asset testifies nowhere; and search the compound as a building that has already shown us exactly one of its faces — the welcoming one.

researchDesk.title: Waluigi’s After-Hours Research Desk
researchDesk.intro: The verdict above is filed. These optional one-shot checks pull three loose threads without pretending the dice can rewrite the night. A breakthrough sharpens the invitation reading; a dead end files the limit of what I can honestly claim.

rolls.title: Audit the maintenance trail
rolls.prompt: Set the silent hinges beside the unmanned wall-walk and ask what nightly traffic the annex pretends not to have.
rolls.success: Breakthrough: a used gate with no watchers is not an unguarded gate — it is a gate whose watchers were stood down. Somebody cleared that wall-walk before I arrived, and cleared schedules leave rosters.
rolls.failure: Useful limit: I can show the gate was used and unwatched, but this file cannot name who oiled it or when. The maintenance log I want does not exist in any archive I can reach.

rolls.title: Compare the two gate admissions
rolls.prompt: Lay my button-and-insult admission beside the asset’s smile-and-silence admission and ask what checkpoint has two ceremonies.
rolls.success: Breakthrough: checkpoints have one procedure and corrupt ones have none — two distinct ceremonies means two distinct orders. My cue was the slammed hand; its credential was its face. The gate processed us, it did not fail us.
rolls.failure: Useful limit: the contrast is suggestive but not conclusive. A lazy guard and a familiar face could produce the same two speeds without any standing orders at all.

rolls.title: Read the burst direction
rolls.prompt: Take the outward burst, the missing repair order, and the office silence together and ask what a planned exit costs.
rolls.success: Breakthrough: planned exits are cheap and unplanned breaches are paperwork — and there is no paperwork. No repair order, no incident report, no statement. The compound did not report the wall because the wall did what it was meant to do.
rolls.failure: Useful limit: silence proves little by itself. Bowser’s office ignores plenty of real damage for reasons of pride, backlog, or spite, and I cannot separate those from design on this evidence.

analyses.title: The Brothers' Argument, Line by Line
analyses.subtitle: A primary source at last - and read one line at a time, the fight is not about Mario at all
analyses.filed: 20 Harvestide, 1035 BF - two days after the Star Hill clinic delivery - filed from the chair, before I left the room. Revised same week, once a cleaner dub of the tape surfaced and I heard how much I had missed the first time. An auditor who does not correct his own filing is not an auditor, he is a fan.
analyses.summary: The archive has carried this argument for two filings on the word of a blue-painted impostor who was not in the room. There is now a tape, and a fuller dub of it than I had the first time I filed this. Read line by line it is not a fight about betrayal, or about Koopa, or even about Peach - it is a fight about being SEEN, and Mario loses it because he keeps answering the wrong question.
analyses.thesis:
Every previous reading of this argument - mine included, in my own first pass at this very tape - treated it as a corruption story. Koopa got to Luigi, Luigi turned, Mario tried to reach him. That reading is comfortable and it is wrong, and the tape proves it wrong in the first exchange.

Luigi opens with *you thought that Koopa worked alone*. That is not a confession of being corrupted. It is a boast about having been UNDERESTIMATED - and it is addressed to a brother who, by Luigi's account, has spent a lifetime doing exactly that. Read the whole tape with that as the subject and every line lands differently. Luigi never once asks Mario to atone for a crime. He asks, in a dozen different ways, to be *acknowledged*. And Mario - who is not a cruel man and is trying his whole heart here - answers nearly every one of them with the bond instead of the grievance. *You're my brother. We're family. It's-a we.* He plays that card so many times across this tape that I lost count on my first filing and have had to recount on this one.

Mario is defending the relationship. Luigi is prosecuting its terms. They are not having the same argument, and that - not Koopa, not Peach, not the Cape Feather at the end - is why it ends where it ends.

sections.heading: Line 1-2: The Boast, and the Answer That Misses It
sections.sourceAnchor:
**LUIGI:** *You thought that Koopa worked alone...*

**MARIO:** *Luigi What do you mean by that? I've a fought too much And you stand against me! Think of the days That were all lead astray Your my brother That's not, Something that'll go away.*
sections.body:
Everything is in the first two lines, so I am going to spend longer here than anywhere else.

**Luigi's line is a boast, not a confession.** A corrupted man's first sentence is *he made me* or *you don't understand* or nothing at all. Luigi's is *you thought* - a sentence built to put his brother on the wrong side of a fact he should already have known. It requires an audience expected to be impressed. It is a credential being presented.

**Mario's reply contains five separate moves and not one of them is the right one.** He asks what Luigi means - stalling. He cites his own effort: *I've a fought too much*. He names the offence as positional: *you stand against me*. He reaches for *Think of the days That were all lead astray* - and then, finally, the bond: *Your my brother*.

I missed that fourth move on my first filing and it matters more than the others. *Think of the days* is Mario reaching for the past as evidence, in the plural, the same way an accountant reaches for a ledger. Two lines later Luigi will reach for the exact same currency and rule the opposite way - *all of the days That I was cast away*. Neither brother invented that method independently. They have been keeping the same book for years and arriving at opposite totals.

Mark the last move, too. Twelve seconds in, Mario has already played the bond card. He will play it many more times across this tape - I have counted, and I will keep count as we go - and it does not work once. Note also *That's not, Something that'll go away* - he is treating the brotherhood as a fact of nature that survives regardless of conduct. Luigi is about to argue that it is a contract with terms. **That is the whole fight and it is fully formed before either man raises his voice.**

sections.heading: Line 3-5: "Only in the Way" - the Complaint Is Geometric
sections.sourceAnchor:
**LUIGI:** *you've done enough off the cuff*

**MARIO:** *Is-a that clear?*

**LUIGI:** *Call my bluff ill rebuff Standing my ground here all of the days That I was cast away What's a brother if he's Only in the way!*
sections.body:
*You've done enough off the cuff* is an accusation of carelessness, not malice. Luigi is not saying Mario hurt him deliberately. He is saying Mario did it without thinking, which is worse, because it means it cost Mario nothing.

**Mario's *Is-a that clear?* is the single worst line he speaks on this tape.** Three words, and every one of them is a man asking to be agreed with. He has just been told his conduct was thoughtless and his response is to check whether his own point landed. He is not listening. He is waiting.

Then Luigi gives the thesis of his entire case: ***What's a brother if he's Only in the way.*** Read the construction. Not *if he's cruel*. Not *if he lies*. Not *if he abandons you*. If he is **in the way** - a spatial complaint, an obstruction. That is what you call a person who has stood between you and something for so long that you have stopped seeing them as a person and started seeing them as terrain.

And *all of the days That I was cast away* dates the grievance - and answers Mario's own *think of the days* from twelve seconds earlier, item for item, in the negative. **This predates Koopa by years and Luigi has just said so out loud, twice now, in the fifth line of the recording.**

sections.heading: First Overlap: the Damsel Line Is a Feint
sections.sourceAnchor:
*[Both talking over each other]*

**MARIO:** *This-a can't-a be The heroic ending You've dreamed of so please Lets-a go! end-a the show! Luigi just see through All of your spitefilled visions!*

**LUIGI:** *I've gone too far To give up now! For all that I cherish you must-a perish You've stolen All that I've dreamed of and just for-a Clueless damsel!*

**MARIO:** *That's not true And you-a know it! I won't lay you askew! I will face this with you!*

**LUIGI:** *Left in the dimming light Only set to fight The one who has been Holding me back!*
sections.body:
The tape marks this as overlapping speech, and the overlap is the point: from here until it clears, neither man hears a complete sentence from the other.

**Mario is arguing about the ENDING.** *The heroic ending you've dreamed of.* He has cast this as a story with a shape, and he is objecting to how it finishes. Luigi is not arguing about the ending. Luigi is arguing about the entire middle - every day of it.

I want to flag *Lets-a go! end-a the show!* on this revision, because I skipped past it the first time and it is doing real work. Mario calls this a **show** - unprompted, before Luigi has said one word about audiences or being watched. Whatever Luigi is about to accuse him of, across the whole rest of this tape, involves exactly that charge: that Mario narrates, that Mario performs, that everyone is watching Mario and nobody was ever watching Luigi. Mario hands Luigi the word himself, three lines early. I do not think he heard himself do it.

And Luigi's *I've gone too far To give up now* is a man describing a decision already made and regretted only at the edges, not a man persuading himself in real time. Set beside it: *For all that I cherish you must-a perish.* Love and sentence, same breath, no seam between them. I have filed a great many confessions in this archive. Very few keep both halves of that sentence that close together without flinching.

**The damsel line is a decoy and I recognise the technique because I have used it.** You lead with the grievance that makes you sound ordinary, because the real one makes you sound small. Jealousy over a woman comes pre-loaded with sympathy and a recognisable shape. *Nobody ever measured me* comes with none of that; it just sits there being pathetic and true. So Luigi puts the decoy in front, and Mario - not stupid, but listening for the story he already knows - takes it every time.

Then Luigi drops the decoy himself: ***The one who has been Holding me back.*** Not *the one who took her*. There is the real charge, said plainly, in the middle of a passage where Mario cannot hear it because they are both talking.

And Mario's *I will face this with you* is the bond again. Second card, same card.

sections.heading: "I've Given My Life To A Zero" - and the Hinge Question
sections.sourceAnchor:
**LUIGI:** *I'm overzealous, I'm-a not-a jealous! This is the outcome I've reached, therefrom! I've given, My life to. A zero, And that's true.*

**MARIO:** *What must I do? Give my life up to you? Fatal flaws retribute All of my raw mistakes Our bond is torn A regal pain I endure*

**LUIGI:** *Who are you to tell me YOUR TRUTH*

**MARIO:** *Fading away the brothership that soared far!*
sections.body:
***I'm overzealous, I'm-a not-a jealous.*** He denies the decoy himself, unprompted, roughly ninety seconds after deploying it. He is correcting the record even mid-argument, which tells you how badly he wants the real charge understood.

Before the zero line proper, listen to the word Luigi reaches for: ***therefrom.*** Not a rhyme-forced filler. That is a man presenting his resentment as a finding - a conclusion reached, not a feeling that arrived. I recognise the register because it is mine. It is the language of somebody who has been keeping his own file on this for longer than anyone else knew he was keeping one.

***I've given, My life to. A zero.*** The broken metre is doing work here - the line stumbles exactly where the feeling is. And note who the zero is. Not Mario. **Himself.** Luigi has spent a life in service of an outcome and the outcome is that he amounts to nothing. That is not jealousy. That is an audit.

Set against that, Mario's *Fatal flaws retribute All of my raw mistakes* is the vaguest sentence he speaks on the whole tape - flaws, mistakes, no dates, no names, no specifics whatsoever. **Luigi itemises. Mario generalises.** That gap is the argument in miniature: one brother is holding a ledger, the other is holding a feeling, and they keep mistaking that difference for a difference of opinion.

Mario continues with ***What must I do? Give my life up to you?*** - which converts a complaint about recognition into a demand for sacrifice, because sacrifice is a thing Mario knows how to do. He does not know how to do acknowledgement. And *A regal pain I endure* centres his own suffering at the precise moment Luigi has finished describing his.

Then: ***Who are you to tell me YOUR TRUTH.*** This is the hinge of the first half. Luigi is rejecting Mario's standing to narrate - not his facts, his *authority*. Mario has been the one who says what happened for their entire shared life, and Luigi has just revoked the licence.

sections.heading: The Air Clears: "Finally Awakened TO MOCKERY"
sections.sourceAnchor:
*[no longer talking over each other]*

**MARIO:** *Listen for a moment! Just hear me! End-a all the torment All the foes We've come across We stood together Showed them who's the boss*

**LUIGI:** *Finally awakened TO MOCKERY My name has been lost and Unmarked To be the one You'll step upon I'll give myself the boost TO GO BEYOND!*
sections.body:
The tape explicitly marks the overlap ending. For the first time both men can hear each other completely, and **it makes things worse, not better** - which is the most damning structural fact on this recording. The confusion was not the problem. Clarity does not fix it.

Mario's case, stated cleanly at last, opens with *End-a all the torment* before it gets anywhere near *we stood together*. Worth flagging on its own: he names the **argument itself** as the wound he wants healed, not whatever produced it. He wants the fighting to stop hurting. Luigi wants the fact underneath the fighting acknowledged. Asking for the first will never satisfy a man asking for the second, and Mario asks for the first four more times before this tape is over.

*We stood together* - a shared history argument. He is offering the past as evidence that the present is a mistake.

Luigi's reply accepts every fact and rejects the conclusion. ***My name has been lost and Unmarked.*** Unmarked. Not defeated, not wronged - **unrecorded.** I want to be careful here because I am an archivist and I am aware of what I am about to say, but: Luigi's stated injury is a filing error. He was there for all of it and none of it has his name on it.

*To be the one You'll step upon* - the geometry again. He is not describing a rival. He is describing a stair.

And *TO GO BEYOND* in capitals is the first time on this tape that Luigi describes wanting something rather than resenting something.

sections.heading: Second Overlap: "Surpass" Enters the Record
sections.sourceAnchor:
**MARIO:** *You don't truly mean that! Luigi just take a step back! Gain your cool And lose the fool That's making you fall From the tree!*

*[Both talking over each other]*

**LUIGI:** *It's too much too ask you? After I'll surpass you! Buried lies in Hate filled skies Has brought you and I Onto our KNEES!*

**MARIO:** *My bro, we're family! I know that, you see! I don't want you to Be without me!*
sections.body:
***You don't truly mean that*** is Mario telling Luigi what Luigi means. Directly after Luigi revoked his authority to do exactly that. Mario cannot stop; it is reflex.

*Lose the fool That's making you fall From the tree* - Mario is still looking for the external agent. There must be a fool, a Koopa, a corrupting party. The possibility that his brother arrived here on his own reasoning is not available to him.

**And here the real verb finally lands: *surpass*.** Not *destroy*, not *replace*, not *punish*. Surpass. It is a competitive word, not a hateful one, and it will come back at the end of this tape in both their mouths at once.

*Has brought you and I Onto our KNEES* is worth flagging as the one moment, this early, that Luigi describes the damage as mutual.

Mario's answer: ***we're family.*** Card again. And then the tell of the whole recording - ***I don't want you to Be without me.*** Not *I don't want to lose you*. He has framed the loss as Luigi's deprivation. Even his plea is arranged around his own centrality, and he does not hear himself do it.

sections.heading: Shouting: Mario Blames Koopa, Luigi Charges Him Interest
sections.sourceAnchor:
*[both start intense shouting]*

**MARIO:** *Behind of this Masquerade I know you still love me! Koopa made you go insane I'll help relieve the strain! Displease!*

**LUIGI:** *Was it worth the fees? Gave your heart a squeeze! You've shunned my displease*
sections.body:
Mario says it outright at last: ***Koopa made you go insane.*** This is the reading the archive has been running on for two filings, and here is the man himself supplying it - **as a hope, in the middle of shouting, with no evidence offered.** It is not analysis. It is the least frightening available explanation, reached for by someone who needs one.

*Behind of this Masquerade I know you still love me.* He is insisting the real Luigi is elsewhere, intact, and that the man in front of him is a costume. That is a profound refusal to credit his brother with his own actions. **Even Luigi's villainy has to belong to somebody else.**

Luigi's reply is the sharpest counter on the tape: ***Was it worth the fees?*** He has priced it. He is treating a lifetime of standing behind his brother as an invoice that was never settled, and asking whether the payer thinks he got value.

*You've shunned my displease* - clumsy, and I am leaving it exactly as spoken. He is saying: you did not even do me the courtesy of taking my objection seriously. **Shunned. Not refused. Not argued with. Declined to acknowledge.** It is the same complaint as line five, eleven exchanges later, and Mario still has not touched it.

sections.heading: The Silhouette Passage - and the Witness at the Window
sections.sourceAnchor:
*[only silhouettes of both of them; a shadow of Peach watches from beyond a window]*

**LUIGI:** *"Luigi and Mario," "What a major duo!"*

**MARIO:** *You know that's true Just me and you,*

**LUIGI:** *If it only it weren't a dream*

**MARIO:** *damn it luigi!*

**LUIGI:** *I, wouldn't be the fiend!*
sections.body:
This is the tenderest passage on the tape and it is the one I trust least, for reasons that have nothing to do with the brothers.

**The content first.** Luigi quotes something - the quotation marks are audible in his delivery. *"Luigi and Mario." "What a major duo!"* He is reciting how they were once described, with his own name first, and the citation is the injury: that is the only place the billing ever ran in that order. Mario answers *Just me and you* - the bond, again. And Luigi's *If it only it weren't a dream* concedes, for one line, that he wanted it to be real.

***damn it luigi*** is the only thing Mario says on this entire recording in his own unguarded voice. No accent written in, no rhyme, no metre, lowercase. **When Mario finally stops performing, what comes out is not an argument. It is exhaustion.**

**Now the problem.** Three things about the silhouette treatment are not consistent with tape damage. It begins on a sentence boundary and ends on one. It obscures the two men in the foreground and does *not* obscure the window behind them, which stays legible throughout. And the audio does not degrade with it - the voices come through this passage cleaner than thirty seconds earlier.

Damage does not have taste. **Somebody composited this.** And whoever did it either did it to hide the brothers, or to ensure the only clearly readable thing in frame was the third figure at the window. Those are opposite intentions producing an identical image, and I will not guess between them in a document with my name on it.

**The archive has never interviewed the watcher.** She was there. She saw it. Nobody has asked her a single question.

sections.heading: The Hinge: "BECAUSE YOUR MY BROTHER" / "NO LONGER MY BROTHER"
sections.sourceAnchor:
*[fade back in; Mario sweating, Luigi standing firm, shadow gone]*

**MARIO:** *Memories shared The duo not impaired Showing that I cared BECAUSE YOUR MY BROTHER*

**LUIGI:** *Sparked inside me Was the pain you seldom And now you plea? you are NO LONGER MY BROTHER!*

**MARIO:** *This is trickery! You would never be Fooled by that Koopa fiend*

**LUIGI:** *YOU DAMN FOOL Let-a this tale end*
sections.body:
Note the staging on the return: **Mario sweating, Luigi standing firm.** Whatever happened under the silhouette cost Mario something and cost Luigi nothing.

Mario plays the bond card again, in capitals this time: ***BECAUSE YOUR MY BROTHER.*** He does not know yet that he has one more play left in him after this - I will get to that shortly - but in this moment it is his loudest, and it is loudest because he can feel it slipping the instant before it is formally taken from him.

***you are NO LONGER MY BROTHER.*** **This is the only line on the entire tape that changes a status rather than describing one.** Everything before it is two men disputing an account of the past. After it there is a new fact in the world that was not there ninety seconds earlier, and it was created by being said out loud. Luigi does not refute the bond. He *terminates* it - accepting its existence in order to end it, which is a far more deliberate act than denial.

*Sparked inside me Was the pain you seldom* - broken again, and again broken exactly where it hurts. *The pain you seldom* [acknowledged]. The sentence cannot finish because the verb is the thing he has never once received.

And Mario's response to a formal revocation is ***This is trickery*** - Koopa, again, immediately. He does not adapt. **He cannot.** The archive should sit with how frightening that is in a man otherwise famous for improvising his way out of anything.

sections.heading: "My Own Shine Dimmed Far Blind" - the Real Grievance, Finally Plain
sections.sourceAnchor:
**MARIO:** *this just can't-*

**LUIGI:** *Burned beyond the bend Show me that glee Oh, across from me galaxies Saved by you Shadowed me What's to see? My own shine Dimmed far blind*

**MARIO:** *Facing the climax Wishing to backtrack It's just a setback A minor blowback! Stuck in a false dream Wishing to redeem*

**LUIGI:** *Mario its-a you Wishing the climax Facing a masked rat "It's just a setback" "A minor blowback" ending your regime Far-a since redeemed*
sections.body:
**Mario does not even finish his sentence here.** *this just can't-* - and Luigi is over him. Every earlier interruption on this tape happened inside a marked overlap, both men shouting past each other in a mess the tape itself flags as noise. This one is clean. Luigi simply does not permit the sentence to complete, and what he delivers instead is the single most complete piece of testimony on the whole recording.

***Galaxies Saved by you Shadowed me.*** There it is with nothing in front of it. Not *you took her*, not *you wronged me* - **you saved galaxies and the saving cast a shadow and I have been standing in it.** Luigi's complaint is not that Mario did wrong. It is that Mario did *right*, enormously, repeatedly, and that the light of it blinded everyone to the man standing beside him.

*My own shine Dimmed far blind.* He is not claiming he had none. He is claiming it could not be seen. **That is a completely different accusation and the archive has never once filed it correctly.**

Then watch what Luigi does with Mario's words. Mario offers comfort - *it's just a setback, a minor blowback* - and Luigi **repeats it back inside quotation marks.** He is not misunderstanding Mario. He is quoting him to his face to demonstrate how small the comfort sounds from where he is standing. It is the most sophisticated rhetorical move either brother makes on this tape, and it is Luigi who makes it.

*Facing a masked rat* - and note, Luigi now applies the masquerade language to *Mario*. Each brother has spent this recording accusing the other of being a costume.

sections.heading: "It's-a We" - the Last Card, Played After It's Already Been Voided
sections.sourceAnchor:
**MARIO:** *Step every per diem Hear my pleas! Galaxies, saved by you, And-a me Can't you see? your own shine*

**LUIGI:** *So why not and Crush your dreams!*

**MARIO:** *Luigi, It's-a we!*
sections.body:
I nearly filed past this exchange entirely the first time, which I am not proud of, because it may be the cruellest three lines on the whole tape.

Listen to what Mario does with Luigi's own sentence. Luigi has just said *my own shine, dimmed far blind* - a claim about a light that could not be seen because it was standing next to a bigger one. Mario's answer is to take that exact phrase and edit a co-author into it: *Galaxies, saved by you, And-a me... your own shine.* He is not disputing the complaint. He is rewriting it, live, to include himself in the very sentence about being erased. That is either the most tone-deaf thing Mario does on this tape or the most honest, and I genuinely cannot rule between the two: I do not think he can help it. Sharing credit is the only language he has.

*So why not and Crush your dreams!* is the flattest, least decorated line Luigi speaks in the whole recording - no wordplay, no ledger, no itemised grievance. Just refusal, plain. He has stopped arguing his case and started answering the only way left.

And then Mario, down to two words: ***It's-a we.*** This is the bond card again, and by my count it is the last one he plays - and he plays it *after* Luigi has already formally ended the brotherhood two passages earlier. He is not arguing anymore either. He is just saying the word into a room where it has already been ruled inadmissible.

sections.heading: "Are We-a Still Superstars?" - Four Seconds of Perfect Agreement
sections.sourceAnchor:
**MARIO:** *The chance to surpass* / **LUIGI:** *The chance to surpass*

**MARIO:** *Are-* / **LUIGI:** *Are-*

**BOTH:** *Are we-a still superstars?*

**BOTH:** *Even in the face of whats been torn asunder*

**LUIGI:** *I've-a gone and lost the faith* / **MARIO:** *Am I gonna lose the faith* / **MARIO:** *Inside my brother?* / **LUIGI:** *Inside my brother,*
sections.body:
**This is the only stretch of the recording where neither man interrupts the other, and it is the clearest proof that the conversation had already failed.**

They converge on identical vocabulary. *The chance to surpass*, together. *Are-*, together. Then a shared line. Agreement on the words is exactly what allows two people to walk away each certain they were understood, and they mean opposite things by every syllable of it. Mario's *surpass* is a thing brothers do for each other. Luigi's is a thing he must do *to* Mario.

Then the tense does all the work, and I want this noted precisely because it is the finest detail on the tape:

**Luigi: *I've-a gone and lost the faith.*** Past. Completed. It is done, it happened some time ago, and he is reporting it.

**Mario: *Am I gonna lose the faith.*** Future. Interrogative. He is still asking whether this is going to happen.

One of them is describing a completed loss and the other is worrying about a possible one, **in the same breath, in the same sentence, sharing the same object.** Mario is not in the same conversation. He has never been in the same conversation. And *Inside my brother* is spoken by both of them - Mario as a question, Luigi as a full stop.

***Are we-a still superstars?*** is the saddest line in this archive and I am filing that as a finding.

sections.heading: "So!" / "No!" - Where It Stops Being an Argument
sections.sourceAnchor:
**LUIGI:** *So!* / **MARIO:** *No!*

**LUIGI:** *WHY WON'T YOU DIE!*
sections.body:
Two syllables each, and the conversation ends here. Everything after this point is not persuasion.

*So!* is Luigi drawing a conclusion. *No!* is Mario refusing the conclusion rather than the premise - **still, after everything, arguing with the outcome instead of the case.**

Then: ***WHY WON'T YOU DIE.***

I have listened to this line more times than is healthy and I am going to record the reading I keep arriving at, with the caveat that it is a reading. It is phrased as a **complaint about failure**, not as a declaration of intent. *Why won't you* is what you say when something you have been attempting is not working. It is the grammar of frustration, not of murder.

**Which means the attempts came first, before this tape.** That sentence implies a history the archive does not have. On the fuller dub I now have in front of me, the very next lines stop implying it and start confirming it - see below.

sections.heading: "DEATH" / "FATE" - and Who Chose Where This Ends
sections.sourceAnchor:
**LUIGI:** *I've had enough Of this kid's scuff No more weak bluffs FACE your beloved Useless praying to the sky set in stone that YOU WILL DIE*

**MARIO:** *I still got hope in you Something Could change within you This-a mess is growing dire*

**LUIGI:** *Raising the heat! I refuse to beaten! I will give my last breath*

**MARIO:** *Rising demand Escalating your plan Oh, dear bro forgive me!*

**MARIO:** *I just couldn't change your* - **LUIGI:** *IF IT RESULTS IN YOUR* - **LUIGI:** *DEATH* / **MARIO:** *FATE*

*[Mario is shown with a Cape Feather; a sound is heard; the feed cuts out]*
sections.body:
This is the section I most regret filing thin the first time. The fuller dub adds three lines and they change the ending.

*No more weak bluffs FACE your beloved Useless praying to the sky* - Luigi names Mario's hope and dismisses it as prayer, **before Mario has said a word about hope.** And then, exactly as forecast, Mario says it: *I still got hope in you.* He walks directly into the description Luigi just gave of him. I do not think that is coincidence and I do not think it is scripted irony either - I think it is simply what happens when one brother has spent the whole tape being audited by someone who has clearly rehearsed this in his head many times before pressing record on his own resentment, so to speak.

*This-a mess is growing dire* is worth setting beside *damn it luigi* from the silhouette passage - the second time on this tape Mario drops the performance entirely and just names the scale of what is happening, plainly, without a card to play.

**The line I missed entirely on my first filing is Luigi's: *Raising the heat! I refuse to beaten! I will give my last breath.*** This is the second moment on the whole tape - after *has brought you and I onto our knees* - where Luigi frames the cost as falling on both of them, not just on Mario. *My last breath* is not a threat aimed outward. It is a wager he is willing to lose himself. Taken together with *why won't you die*, this closes the question the break section left open: the attempts were not only prior to this tape, they are still actively underway *during* it, stated outright, by the man making them.

**Mario's last full line is an apology.** *Oh, dear bro forgive me.* He is asking forgiveness immediately before doing something, which means he has decided to do it and knows what it is. That is the only moment on this tape where Mario is ahead of Luigi rather than behind him.

And then the final construction, which is the most deliberate piece of writing in the whole recording. Two half-sentences, interleaved, completing on a single shared beat:

**Mario: *I just couldn't change your... FATE.*** **Luigi: *IF IT RESULTS IN YOUR... DEATH.***

Same grammatical slot. Same instant. One word each. **DEATH and FATE are the same syllable count and the opposite claim** - Luigi names an act, Mario names an inevitability he is absolving himself of. They are still, in the last word either of them speaks, having two different arguments.

**Now the part I cannot resolve.** The final frame holds a Cape Feather. A sound is heard. The feed does not fade and does not tear - it *stops*, between one frame and the next, with the audio cut clean.

A tape that runs out does not stop in silence. It stops mid-word, with noise on the tail. **This one ends on a held breath, on a visible object, immediately after the most quotable line in the recording.** That is an ending somebody wrote.

So the archive carries two open items against this document, and I file both as open rather than pretend either is resolved: **an uninterviewed witness at the window, and an unidentified editor** with access to the master, a compositing suite, and an opinion about where the story should end.

**Until I have names for those two, every line above is a reading of something I was handed rather than something I found.**

analyses.verdict:
My verdict is unchanged by the fuller dub, and strengthened by it: this is not a corruption story and we should stop filing it as one.

Luigi is not a good man who was got at. He is a man with a real and long-standing grievance - that he was never credited, never seen, never counted - who has chosen an unforgivable way to force the issue. Koopa did not install that grievance. Koopa found it already there and gave it somewhere to go. Mario's insistence otherwise, right to the last line, is the most loving and the most damaging thing he does all night, because it is one more refusal to grant his brother authorship of his own life. He plays the bond card so many times I have twice lost count filing this, and the last time - It's-a we, two words, after the brotherhood has already been formally revoked - may be the single most heartbreaking thing on the entire tape.

The new lines also close a gap I left open the first time. I wrote that WHY WON'T YOU DIE reads as frustration rather than intent, and implies attempts prior to the tape. Raising the heat! I refuse to beaten! I will give my last breath does not merely imply that history. It states it, in the present tense, mid-argument, from the man making the attempt. I am updating the file accordingly rather than pretending my first reading already covered it.

Two items remain in the open file. There is a witness at the window who has never been interviewed. And there is an editor - somebody cut this tape, chose the silhouette passage, and chose the ending - who is currently the single most important unidentified person in this investigation.

I have now watched this more times than I am willing to put a number to. It does not change. That is not the same as it being finished.
