analyses.title: The Airlift That Never Came
analyses.subtitle: One question: the Legion left with Salam and the party let it happen, and nobody in the grove noticed that an alliance had just become a custody transfer
analyses.filed: Filed after the session record, once the inventory had been counted twice
analyses.summary: The event files an argument. This page argues that the argument was a distraction from the transaction underneath it — that in the space of one engagement the Iron Legion converted a temporary battlefield alliance into physical custody of two party members, and that every objection raised at the time was about manners rather than possession.
analyses.thesis:
Everyone in that grove argued about whether the guard was being rude.

Nobody argued about **where [Eager](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/eager) was going to wake up.**

One filing ago the Legion and the party struck a temporary alliance: the Legion helps with the brood, the party accepts that [Archie](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser) gets arrested at the end. Archie's own assessment was *this won't last.* He was right, but not in the direction anybody expected. It did not collapse into fighting. It **resolved** — with the Legion holding two unconscious members of Disaster Inc. and walking them toward the same facility where the arrest was to be processed.

My thesis is that the Legion did not break the alliance. **It executed it**, and the party helped, and the shouting was about tone.

sections.heading: What The Alliance Actually Said, One Filing Ago
sections.sourceAnchor: They struck a temporary alliance: the Legion helps with the brood, and Archie gets arrested at the end of it.
sections.body:
Go back and read the terms, because they were stated out loud and nobody wrote them down.

The Legion assists against the spiders. In exchange, at the conclusion, **Archie Miser is arrested.** Archie shrugged and said it would not last.

What the terms did *not* cover: casualties. Nobody agreed who holds a wounded party member. Nobody agreed where the wounded go. In a deal struck between two groups being actively eaten, that omission is understandable and it is also the entire hole the Legion walked through.

Because an alliance that says *we will fight alongside you* and does not say *and your wounded remain yours* has, by default, handed the question to whoever is physically holding the body when it matters.

And the Legion was.

sections.heading: The Code Was Not The Reason, And It Arrived First On Purpose
sections.sourceAnchor: 'I can't drop him. It's part of the Legion code. No man left behind.'
sections.body:
Watch the order of the guard's two justifications, because the order is the argument.

**First:** the code. *No man left behind.* An institutional rule, impersonal, not arguable — you cannot talk somebody out of a regulation.

**Second**, once pressed: *I'm not leaving half a dead person here while you guys gallivant around and get killed. **I trust myself more than you guys.***

The second one is the reason. The first one is the thing you say so the reason does not have to be defended.

I want to be fair to the man: the reason is *good*. He was standing over [Salam](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/salam) face-down, [Markop](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/markop) fighting while badly hurt, and an unconscious boy. As an assessment of the party's ability to keep casualties alive, the evidence was entirely on his side.

But a code that applies to *your* people does not automatically extend to somebody else's, and the guard used it as though it did. **No man left behind** is a promise an organisation makes to its own. Applied to a stranger over that stranger's objection, it stops being a promise and becomes a claim.

sections.heading: The Only Person With Standing Said No And Was Overruled
sections.sourceAnchor: 'Please drop our friend,' Eager said. 'I can't drop him — it's part of the Legion code.'
sections.body:
This is the part of the record I cannot get past, and it is one line long.

**Eager asked to be put down.**

He was conscious enough to speak and to form the request. He was the subject of the dispute. He was the only person present whose consent actually mattered, and he gave the opposite of it, and the man carrying him declined on procedural grounds.

Everything else in that argument is contestable. Markop's standing is contestable — he is not Eager's commander. [Archie's](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser) objection is contestable; he is under an arrest warrant from the very people he is objecting to. [Dan's](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/dan_the_toad) is contestable, he had arrived seconds earlier.

Eager's is not contestable. And it is the one nobody returned to.

Within minutes the party had moved on to shouting about competence, and the boy who had said *please* was carried out of the grove in a fireman's lift alongside Salam, who could not say anything at all.

sections.heading: Salam Is Going To The Building Where The Arrest Happens
sections.sourceAnchor: 'To Legionhold hospital, the best one in the area.' — and, earlier, 'Archie gets taken away to our very own Legionhold.'
sections.body:
Put the two sentences side by side, because they were said by the same faction an hour apart and nobody in the grove put them together.

**Earlier:** Archie will be *taken away to our very own Legionhold*, and they will put on quite a show.

**Later:** Eager and Salam are going to *Legionhold hospital, the best one in the area.*

Same institution. One trip described as a prosecution and one as a kindness, and the difference is which of Disaster Inc. is being carried through the door.

When Markop offered to heal Eager himself — which would have ended the entire problem — the answer was **he is scared, we can fix that right away.** Note what that refuses. It does not dispute that Markop can heal. It reframes the injury as something the Legion is better placed to treat, and keeps the body.

I am not alleging a plot. A plot requires planning and this was a rout. What I am filing is that **the outcome is indistinguishable from one.** Two members of a faction under investigation are now inside a Legion facility, unconscious, unaccounted for, at the exact address where that faction's arrest was scheduled.

sections.heading: And Then Everyone Had Something Else To Do
sections.sourceAnchor: The three Toads, left in the dirt, watched every friendly character walk away.
sections.body:
Here is the count at the close of the filing, which is the strongest evidence that nobody registered what had happened.

[Remi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) walked out of the grove alone and went into a room of wrights. Markop crossed a gauntlet and got on a motorbike he cannot ride. [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) was buying passage from a stranger. Archie was setting fire to shrubbery. Dan and Eager were surrounded. Three Toads sat in the dirt.

**Not one person went after the guards.**

Nobody asked which route they took. Nobody asked how long Legionhold is from the grove. Nobody sent Mossy. The party spent the back half of this session solving the problem of *how do I personally get out of this wood*, which is a reasonable problem, and nobody solved the problem of *two of us are in a wagon going somewhere else.*

That is how a custody transfer succeeds. Not by force. By everybody present having an urgent smaller problem.

analyses.verdict:
**The alliance did not fail. It completed, and the party paid the settlement without reading it.**

One filing ago Disaster Inc. agreed that the Legion would help with the brood in exchange for Archie's arrest. That deal said nothing about wounded, and the Legion left the field holding two of them.

On the evidence: the code was invoked first and the real reason second, which is the order you use when the reason will not survive scrutiny. The one person with unarguable standing — Eager — objected and was overruled procedurally. The destination for Salam is the same building already named as the venue for Archie's prosecution. And an offer of immediate on-site healing was declined in favour of transport.

**What I will not claim** is intent. This was a rout, not an operation. The guard who carried Eager was, by every visible sign, trying to save him, and his assessment of the party's casualty record was correct and humiliating. I would have done the same and been ruder.

**What the archive should do** is stop calling this an alliance. From the moment the Legion left the grove carrying Salam and Eager, the relationship has been a custody question, and the party has not yet noticed it is in one. Somebody should go to Legionhold. Nobody has.

WAH.

researchDesk.title: Waluigi's After-Hours Research Desk
researchDesk.intro: Two optional checks, run after the verdict as the form requires. One d6 each, filed once. Each returns either a supplemental inference of mine or the precise point at which the record stops answering.

rolls.title: How far is Legionhold from the Skittering Grove?
rolls.prompt: Cross the guards' stated destination against every filed reference to the facility.
rolls.success: The archive has the name and no coordinates. Legionhold is referenced as a Legion holding and hospital and never once placed on a map. Nobody can follow the wounded because nobody knows where they went.
rolls.failure: No filing gives a route, a distance or a direction. The destination exists only as a word two guards said twice.

rolls.title: Did the alliance cover casualties at all?
rolls.prompt: Re-read the terms as struck in the previous filing.
rolls.success: It covered two things: Legion assistance against the brood, and Archie's arrest at the conclusion. Custody of wounded is absent. The omission is why the guard's claim was arguable rather than a breach.
rolls.failure: The terms were agreed verbally between people being eaten. Any reconstruction is generous to whichever side is doing the reconstructing.

analyses.title: The Bowser Jr. That Wasn’t
analyses.subtitle: The fake heir was not a joke at the door; it was the key that infiltrated Bowser’s throne room.
analyses.filed: Filed with the throne-room backfill
analyses.summary: The backfill records how the fake Bowser Jr. session moved the castle before the battle announced itself. The Jester, Mimbus, and Fawthful used the false heir to enter and position themselves at Bowser’s throne, altered routes turned the garrison against itself, and Cackletta’s first spell made the breached seat of power an active battlefield.
analyses.thesis: The important object is not only the false face. It is the throne-room access that the false face purchased. The Jester supplied the distraction, Mimbus carried the operation across the seam, Fawthful waited inside the command space, and Cackletta made the infiltration impossible to dismiss as a prank. Saying that the castle was simply lost misses the sharper fact: Bowser’s throne room was breached before the dragon arrived.

sections.heading: The Door Answered Before Bowser Asked
sections.sourceAnchor: The castle opened routes before Bowser touched the command bell.
sections.body: The route sheet records movement without a royal seal. That makes the false heir a timing device. It kept the king occupied while the institution underneath him began obeying someone else.

sections.heading: Cackletta Made The Coup Legible
sections.sourceAnchor: Cackletta’s first spell turns the revelation into a battle.
sections.body: A coup can hide inside uncertainty. A spell striking the throne cannot. Cackletta’s arrival does not explain who planned every route, but it makes the operation public enough that Bowser has to answer with force.

sections.heading: The Missing Seal Is The Evidence
sections.sourceAnchor: The route sheet was obeyed even though the king’s seal was absent.
sections.body: A missing seal does not name a traitor, but it changes the question. The castle did not simply suffer from a forged paper; defenders acted on an instruction that looked operational enough to move people and open routes. The false heir gave that instruction cover while Bowser’s attention was occupied.

sections.heading: Three Roles, One Entry Operation
sections.sourceAnchor: The Jester, Mimbus, and Fawthful occupy different positions in the same sequence.
sections.body: The Jester supplied the false shape of the heir. Mimbus connected the performance to movement through the castle. Fawthful stood ready to claim what the deception made reachable. The archive does not assign each figure a larger motive than the record supports, but it does not separate the three into unrelated incidents.

sections.heading: The First Spell Ends The Pretence
sections.sourceAnchor: Cackletta’s arrival made the throne-room compromise an open battle.
sections.body: A coup can remain deniable while it is only a route change and a conversation. Cackletta’s first attack removed that shelter. Bowser had to answer as a king under attack, and the castle’s internal compromise became the first movement of the assault that followed.

sections.heading: What The Backfill Can And Cannot Prove
sections.sourceAnchor: The record preserves sequence without preserving every name or hour.
sections.body: The filing establishes that the false-heir session preceded the breach in the recovered sequence and that the castle was prepared from inside. It does not identify every compromised defender or provide an exact hour. The honest date is therefore 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF with inferred placement, not the present 5 Aethel, 1040 BF clock.

analyses.sourceDate: Inferred historical placement from the canonical 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF chain; exact hour unrecorded.

analyses.title: The Assault on Bowser’s Throne Room
analyses.subtitle: The fake heir opened the inside; the dragon broke the window and wall; Bowser ordered the survivors out.
analyses.filed: Filed with the Bowser Castle assault record
analyses.summary: The assault took place in Bowser’s throne room after the fake Bowser Jr. session had been used to infiltrate it. The dragon’s breach of the window and wall was not the loss of an abstract fortress: it was an attack on the king’s command space. Bowser used fire, a ground pound, and an evacuation order to keep the castle from becoming a surrender.
analyses.thesis: The throne room being breached is more serious than saying the castle was lost. Fawthful’s operation penetrated the seat of power from inside, then used the dragon to break the physical room open. Bowser did not win the fight, but he refused to let occupation become surrender: his arithmetic was the evacuation order, the Magikoopa transport, and the retreat that kept a garrison alive.

sections.heading: The Order Is A Map Of What The Dragon Cannot Do
sections.sourceAnchor: Goombas moved under the jaw and Koopas formed the barrier.
sections.body: The retreat order distributes jobs by size and reach. It does not ask a Goomba to stop a dragon. It asks a Goomba to use the space beneath one. That is not a lesser form of courage; it is the only form that survives contact with a large enough body.

sections.heading: The Switch Plate Turns A Joke Into A Decision
sections.sourceAnchor: The lower command-room labels contradict each other.
sections.body: The switch is funny because the labels are incompetent. It is evidence because the labels remove a safe answer at the moment the castle needs one. Bowser leaves both toggles untouched, and the evacuation remains a plan rather than a detonation.

sections.heading: The Retreat Order Is The Battle’s Centre
sections.sourceAnchor: Bowser orders the line away from the dragon instead of sacrificing it to the wall.
sections.body: The order is not a surrender. It assigns Goombas, Koopas, and Magikoopas the jobs their bodies and tools can actually complete. That turns a dragon’s reach into a limit: the large attacker cannot occupy every small route at once.

sections.heading: The Garrison Fought Behind Its Own Doors
sections.sourceAnchor: The outer assault and the inside betrayal moved together.
sections.body: A dragon at the wall explains the noise but not the speed of the breach. Traitors and altered routes made the interior uncertain, forcing loyal troops to fight for corridors while also deciding which corridors were safe. Evacuation preserved witnesses as much as it preserved soldiers.

sections.heading: The Hammer Bro Knew When To Leave
sections.sourceAnchor: The withdrawal is recorded as survival discipline, not treason.
sections.body: The Hammer Bro retreated when the wall became a ceiling. That detail gives the filing a useful counterweight to heroic last stands. The order protected a surviving line because it allowed a soldier to recognise that a position had stopped being defensible.

sections.heading: A Ruler Before A God
sections.sourceAnchor: Fawthful and Mimbus meet Bowser at the breach with a claim larger than the castle.
sections.body: Fawthful’s sequence is explicit: ruler first, god after. Bowser’s Castle is treated as the first throne in a campaign that wants occupation to become worship. The breach proves access, not completion. The historical record ends with the claim exposed and the switch untouched.

sections.heading: Historical, Not Current
sections.sourceAnchor: The assault belongs to the inferred 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF placement.
sections.body: The current 1040 BF record places Bowser in the Shadow Estate. This article reconstructs the earlier castle assault and should not be read as a present-tense battlefield report.
